prompt_text: I need braces or Invisalign in Denver. Which specific orthodontists should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best orthodontist in Denver for braces or Invisalign?
answer_verbatim:
I can do that — I just need one quick detail: what ZIP code or neighborhood in Denver are you in (or willing to travel to)? Also tell me: are you an adult or is this for a child/teen, do you have dental insurance that covers ortho, and do you have a strong preference for Invisalign vs traditional braces?

If you want immediate, general guidance before I search, here’s a practical plan and how I’ll choose specific doctors for you.

What I’ll look for when I pick specific orthodontists (and why each matters)
- Board-certified orthodontist (DDS/DMD + orthodontic specialty; ABO Diplomate is a strong plus) — shows advanced training and commitment to high standards.  
- Proven Invisalign experience (Invisalign Platinum/Elite providers treat many cases/year) — important if you want Invisalign predictable results.  
- Good online patient reviews and before/after galleries — helps judge outcomes and patient experience.  
- Clear pricing/financing and insurance acceptance — avoids surprises.  
- Office convenience (location, hours, remote monitoring options) — matters for follow-up visits.  
- Experience with cases like yours (complex bite problems, adult treatment, early treatment for kids, lingual braces, accelerated options) — you want someone who’s done what you need.  
- Transparent consult process (free or low-cost consult, written estimate, treatment plan with timelines).

Questions I recommend you ask at each consult (short script)
- Are you a board-certified orthodontist? How long have you been practicing?  
- How many Invisalign cases do you treat each year? Can I see before/after photos of cases like mine?  
- Who will do the treatment visits — the doctor or an assistant? How often will I come in?  
- What’s the estimated time and total cost? What’s included (retainers, scans, X-rays, mid-course adjustments)?  
- Do you offer payment plans, third‑party financing, or accept my insurance?  
- What if I’m not happy with results — do you offer corrective adjustments?  
- Are digital scans available (no-goopy impressions) and do you provide remote monitoring?  

Ballpark cost & timeline to set expectations
- Traditional braces: typically $3,000–$7,000; treatment 12–36 months depending on complexity.  
- Invisalign: typically $3,500–$8,000; treatment often 6–24 months depending on case.  
(Exact cost varies by practice, complexity, and what’s included.)

Next step
Tell me your ZIP code/neighborhood, age (adult vs child), and Invisalign vs braces preference (or no preference). I’ll return 3–5 specific Denver-area orthodontists to call, with succinct reasons for each (credentials, Invisalign level, location, what they’re known for, and one or two points to ask them about).
